description: Coal seam fields: one deposit is one minable seam field, tens of km across (300-3,000 km2: a Gillette, Jharia or Newcastle-sized field; not a mine block, not a whole basin) holding a stack of seams; fields adjoin in a basin. Peat mires preserved where accommodation kept pace with peat production, after land plants; rank from burial heating.

source.note: peat-mire facies from the strata log (Bohacs & Suter 1997)

driver.note: accommodation roughly matching peat production; excess drowns mires (Bohacs & Suter 1997); numbers are design

notes: DEFINITION (Ben, decisions log 2026-09-29, "OK; define coal as seams"): one deposit is ONE MINABLE SEAM FIELD, a contiguous area of coal-bearing strata with minable seams, tens of km across: field area 300 / 1,000 / 3,000 km2 (P90 / P50 / P10; about 20-60 km across). Comparable units: the Gillette coalfield (study area ~4,150 km2), India's Gondwana coalfields (Jharia 280-450, Raniganj 440-1,500, North Karanpura 1,230, Singrauli ~2,200 km2 of which ~10 % promising), a Pennsylvania anthracite field (four fields, 1,250 km2 in all, mean 313 km2). Not a mine-sized measured block (Circular 891: measured radius 0.4 km, indicated 1.2 km) and not a whole basin or coal province (Circular 891 glossary: a coal FIELD is 'a discrete area underlain by strata containing one or more coal beds'; a region holds fields, a province holds regions). ESTIMATE, not a USGS figure: no source counts minable seam fields.

DENSITY 4 / 14 / 40 per 100,000 km2 of permissive coal-bearing tract (P90 / P50 / P10; density_basis 'estimate', so the survivor formula uses the P50, 14). Derivation (2026-09-29; research by a Sonnet sub-agent; every field count is a judgement about what to call a field), density = fields / tract area x 1e5: Powder River (Fort Union Formation, 22,000 mi2 = 57,000 km2, PP 1625-A chap. PS; named coalfields Gillette, Sheridan, Decker, Rosebud/Colstrip, Ashland, Glenrock = 6-9 fields): 10.5-15.8. Sydney Basin onshore (36,000 km2, five onshore coalfields; Bioregional Assessments context statement; the tract includes non-coal strata, so this is low): 14-17. Upper Silesia (5,600 km2, three coal areas; the tract is the coal basin itself, so this is a high case): 54. Illinois Basin (~95,000 km2, three state-level fields of 30,000 km2 or more; a low bound): ~3. India (~113 coalfields and occurrences over 3.29 million km2 of land, 34.7 thousand km2 of coalfield; land is not a tract, so this is a floor): 3.4. Geometric check, 1e5 x f / A with f the minable share of the tract and A the field area: f 0.10 with A 3,000 km2 gives 3.3; f 0.25 with A 1,000 gives 25; f 0.5 with A 300 gives 167. P50 14 = the Powder River and Sydney agreement (both ~14), below the geometric median of 25 (14 is f 0.14 at A 1,000 km2); P90 4 = Illinois-style large fields; P10 40 = Silesia-like tracts (fields of 1,500-2,500 km2 filling about half the basin). Above ~60 needs fields under 300 km2 or a tract trimmed to the coal outline. Was 10 / 30 / 80 (placeholder). NOT verified by the research: Illinois Basin 36,800 mi2, Gondwana basin outcrop areas, South African coalfield areas (19 coalfields, SAIMM J. 105(2) p. 95), Bowen Basin area (Geoscience Australia ~160,000 km2, Wikipedia >60,000), Chinese and European coalfield counts.

SOURCES: USGS Circular 891 (Wood et al. 1983) glossary and Table 3; Averitt 1975, USGS Bulletin 1412 (coal-bearing rocks 458,600 mi2 = 13 % of the US; Mammoth bed 3,300 mi2 originally, 484 mi2 preserved in four fields); USGS PP 1625-A chap. PG (Gillette coalfield, 1,026,000 acres) and chap. PS (Fort Union, 22,000 mi2); USGS OFR 2011-1296 Table 1 (Indian coalfields; ~34.7 thousand km2 of coalfield, CFRI 1993); Bioregional Assessments Programme, context statement for the Sydney Basin (36,000 km2 onshore, five coalfields); SAIMM J. 105(2) (South African coalfields); Wikipedia for Upper Silesia (5,400-5,600 km2) and some Indian field areas (weak).

TONNAGE 3,800 / 19,800 / 115,000 Mt (P90 / P50 / P10) = field area x CUMULATIVE minable seam thickness x 1.32 t/m3 (rebased 2026-09-29 when a field became a stack of seams). Area 300 / 1,000 / 3,000 km2; cumulative thickness (the sum of a field's seams, not one bed) 5 / 14 / 60 m, a judgement from the coalfields the stacking research tabulated (cumulative coal, m: Illinois Basin 4.6-14, Appalachian Allegheny Group 6-12, Highveld 6-19, Illawarra 12-20, Witbank 8-32, Powder River net 30-46 in one merged zone, Jharia ~100, Upper Silesia paralic ~137; USGS PP 1625-D, PP 1625-A chap. PS, PP 1708-D1, SAIMM J. 105(2) Table I, Bioregional Assessments, NMET Jharia proposal; several are the research's own arithmetic, see the STATUS entry), the two treated as independent split lognormals and combined by simulation (P10 / P50 / P90 of the product 3,813 / 19,774 / 114,611 Mt). About 15 Mt per km2 at the median, between Upper Silesia (~13) and the Gondwana fields (~110-130); Illinois (1.9) is a basin-wide average. An ESTIMATE, not a USGS distribution. Was 540 / 2,500 / 10,000 Mt with ONE bed's thickness (Circular 891's classes 0.71 / 2.13 / 4.27 m), which a stack of seams outgrows. COE's vein amount follows the site's tonnage QUANTILE in this distribution, so rebasing it does not change amounts.

GEOMETRY: aspect (1, 5.15e-4, 1.5): the field is a cylinder with x : z = 1 : 1.5 whose thickness 2b is the cumulative seam thickness, so at the median tonnage the semi-axes are 14.6 km x 7.5 m x 21.9 km, a 1,000 km2 field with 15 m of coal (29 x 44 km across; 49 x 73 blocks semi-axis at 300 m per block). The engine scales all three axes by the cube root of volume, so P90 gives 334 km2 x 8.7 m and P10 3,230 km2 x 27 m (the area spread is 10x, as sourced). size_mult_h 1: the body IS the field. size_mult_v 20: a metre of coal is a block.

STACK (geometry.stack; Ben, decisions log 2026-09-29, adjoining + stacked): the field holds several parallel seams, written as one body per seam (role ore, consecutive ids, same footprint, yaw and dip), the field's tonnage split across them by thickness (share_sigma 0.7: seam thickness P10-P90 about a factor 7, the research's 0.8-6 m). Count n = round(S / 25 m) clamped to 1-40 and to cumulative thickness / 0.7 m (Circular 891: 28 in, the bituminous reserve-base minimum; no thinner seam is minable), where S is the coal measures the recorded history laid down under the site while its cell was coal-forming: sum over frames of F x deposition x dt, F the cell's favourability (deposition_rate_m_myr and coal_facies are the history's own fields). 25 m of measures per seam and 40 seams at most from the tabulated coalfields (measures per seam: Appalachian Allegheny ~15, Illinois ~11-29, Ruhr 12 for all coals and ~60 for the economic ones, Upper Silesia ~35, Jharia ~19, Highveld 16-60, Illawarra ~27; mineable seams per section: Illinois ~20 mined of 75 named, Llewellyn up to 40, Donets 30-40 workable, Highveld 5, Sydney 4 principal units; Heckel 1986 and Rasbury et al. 1998 cyclothems of 160,000-400,000 yr, about one minable seam per two to four cycles). Gaps between seams: gap_sigma 0.6 (a factor 5 P10-P90, the research's 12-60 m). spacing_mult_v 6 enlarges the gaps in blocks as size_mult_v does thickness (25 m is 1.25 blocks at 20 m per block, too tight to tell seams apart; now 7.5 blocks). The top seam lies half the measures above the ledger's centre depth; erosion drops seams above the ground from the top and clips the one crossing it; the site's tonnage is what is left.

ADJOINING (Ben, decisions log 2026-09-29): sizing.clustering model 'adjoining' and min_separation_m 0: fields fill a basin's minable area, touching but never overlapping in plan (each placed at random in the tract, largest first, where its ellipse crosses none already placed; the yaw is drawn at placement). The camp spacing and Gaussian clustering of the first version (100 / 40 km) are gone for coal.

Density of coal in the ground 1.32 t/m3 for bituminous coal: USGS Circular 891 (Wood et al. 1983), Table 2 p. 22 (1,800 short tons per acre-foot; anthracite 1.47, subbituminous 1.30, lignite 1.29 in data/usgs/coal.json).

PLACEHOLDERS that remain: formation_depth_m 800. The assessment depth is USGS Circular 891's: coal deeper than 6,000 ft (1,800 m) is excluded from resources (printed p. 24, Table 3 p. 14). Design values: the curves, dip, size_mult_v 20.

Rank from Lopatin TTI of the coal layer: TTI 75 <-> Ro ~ 1.1 % (Waples' correspondence as tabulated by the Kansas Geological Survey, non-USGS; the high-volatile bituminous limit). The lignite, subbituminous and low-volatile bounds are PLACEHOLDERS (no USGS table of reflectance by rank was found).
